Class ScalaEnumSerde<E extends scala.reflect.Enum>

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.scala.serde.ScalaEnumSerde<E>
Type Parameters:
E - The enum type
All Implemented Interfaces:
io.micronaut.serde.Deserializer<E>, io.micronaut.serde.Serializer<E>, io.micronaut.serde.util.CustomizableDeserializer<E>, io.micronaut.serde.util.CustomizableSerializer<E>
@Singleton @Requires(classes=io.micronaut.serde.Serializer.class) public final class ScalaEnumSerde<E extends scala.reflect.Enum> extends Object implements io.micronaut.serde.util.CustomizableSerializer<E>, io.micronaut.serde.util.CustomizableDeserializer<E>
Serialization for a Scala 3 enum, which is a name in a document as a Java enum is.

A Scala 3 enum is not a java.lang.Enum unless it says so, so the serializer Micronaut Serialization has for enums does not apply and the case is introspected as a bean instead. The case objects have no properties, so nothing useful comes out and nothing at all goes back in.

The name written is the one the case declares -- its product prefix, not its toString, which an enum may override for display. Reading it back goes through the companion's generated valueOf, which is the same lookup the language itself uses, so a name the enum does not have is rejected here rather than becoming a null the caller meets later.

The type parameter is what makes one bean answer for every enum. A serializer is chosen by what it can accept, so naming scala.reflect.Enum outright would do for writing; a deserializer is chosen by what it can produce, and one that produces scala.reflect.Enum cannot stand in where a particular enum was asked for. Declaring the bound as a type variable instead publishes the bean under a type variable rather than a fixed type, which matches any subtype -- the same device Micronaut Serialization's own enum support uses.
